newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya sells $130 million of treasury bills.
newsitem.headline: Kenya sells $130 million of treasury bills.

text.p: The Central Bank of Kenya sold 7.037 billion shillings ($130 million) of treasury bills at the weekly auction on Thursday, bank officials said.
In the 91-day main category of bills, the bank said it sold 7.031 billion shillings at an average yield of 21.404 percent compared to a yield of 21.450 percent last week.
The yield on the 28-day was unchanged for the third week at 16.754 percent. Only six million shillings were sold compared to 161 million shillings last week.

Commercial bank dealers attributed the increase in demand for the main category of bills to a stable shilling. The shilling has been trading within a narrow band of 54.85/55.00 for the last three weeks.

"We definitely expect an increase in foreign investors looking for treasury bills especially if they can be assured that the tight monetary policy applied by the central bank will continue," one dealer said.
The bank said invited tenders for seven billion shillings of treasury bills for the auction on Thursday next week. ($1=54 shillings)
